description: Basic board control: checking the link (ping), stopping the system safely, restarting, and the communication watchdog (dead-man).

commands.label: Ping
commands.description: Checks that the board answers and returns its uptime in milliseconds.

commands.label: Stop the system
commands.description: Puts the board in its safe state: switches off the device outputs and stops the VM.

commands.label: Restart the board
commands.description: Restarts the ESP32 after the answer is sent (about 100 ms later).

commands.label: Say goodbye
commands.description: The app leaves on purpose (its Disconnect, its window closing): the board turns the dead-man off and goes on with what it runs. Without it a dead-man the app armed would stop the board after the silence that follows. A link that drops without it (power, range) is a lost link as before.

commands.label: Set the clock
commands.description: Gives the board the time (UTC, milliseconds since 1970). The board has no battery clock: the app sets it whenever it connects, and it is lost at a restart.

commands.label: Read the clock
commands.description: The board's time (UTC) and whether a client has set it since the start.

fields.label: Time (UTC)
fields.description: Milliseconds since 1970-01-01 00:00 UTC; counts from 1970 at the start until it is set (before 2020: not a date)

fields.label: Set
fields.description: 1 = the clock holds a date: a client set it (it survives a software restart, not a loss of power)

fields.label: Uptime
fields.description: Time since the board started, the base of the log lines (I (854) tag): with the time above it dates every line

commands.label: Read the safe state
commands.description: Whether the board is in its safe state (the VM stopped, every device output off and suspended), why it entered it and how long ago. A reason of 0: not in it.

fields.label: Reason
fields.description: Why it entered the safe state last; 0 = not in the safe state

commands.label: Leave the safe state
commands.description: Resumes every device (oldest first) and clears the safe state. The program stays stopped: start it with VM EXEC. Motors move again when the devices resume.

commands.label: Set the communication watchdog (dead-man)
commands.description: Sets how long the board waits for a command before it enters its safe state by itself, and whether a lost link does it at once. 0 = off: the board then runs its program on its own, offline, with no client. Runtime only: after a restart the board is as built (off by default).

fields.label: Timeout
fields.description: Time without a command before the safe state (0 = off). The app asks the board about every second while it is connected, so 3000 or more does not trip a connected board; a board with no client is tripped by any value but 0.

fields.label: React to a lost link
fields.description: 1 = enter the safe state at once when the BLE connection drops (the program then stops: leave it off for a board that should keep running without the app)

commands.label: Read the watchdog settings
commands.description: Returns the current timeout and whether a lost link triggers the safe state.
